name: Feedback
summary: Use the Feedback component to give users a consistent, low-distraction route for sharing their experience of a service.
whenToUse: Use on as many service pages as practical when the team has a feedback route it monitors.
Place immediately before the footer so it remains available without distracting from the current task.
whenNotToUse: Do not use when feedback is not reviewed or cannot influence the service.
Do not use it as a replacement for a support route when users need help completing a task.

anatomy.name: Feedback region
anatomy.description: A govuk-feedback container uses the standard width and grid.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.description: A configurable heading identifies the invitation.

anatomy.name: Message and link
anatomy.description: Brief body copy explains why feedback is useful and links to the feedback route.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: The service-wide invitation shown before the footer.

behaviour: The component has no GOV.UK JavaScript behaviour; its link must work without JavaScript.
In the Nunjucks page template, place it in footerStart so document order remains consistent.
Treat this Trial component as changeable and review it on every GOV.UK Frontend update.
accessibility: Set headingLevel so the title fits the page's heading hierarchy.
Make the feedback link purpose clear from its text and surrounding sentence.
Distinguish feedback from urgent help and provide an accessible support route elsewhere.
content: Explain why feedback is requested and what the team will do with it.
Where useful, say how long providing feedback will take and distinguish it from support.
Use a direct label such as “Give us your feedback”.

htmlExamples.name: Service feedback invitation
htmlExamples.html:
Help us improve this service

Tell us about your experience using this service. Give us your feedback
